name: Structural homology
description: Investigate structural correspondence and function-relevant architecture while preserving model origin, matched extent and the limits of structural similarity.
investigation_instructions:
Determine what functions the supplied gene or protein may perform by comparing its structure or relevant structural models with functionally characterized proteins. Start from the supplied sequence, selected file record or region, or snippets; no candidate annotation, public name or pre-existing structure is required. Preserve partial-material limits and establish which target residues any available structure or model represents.

Examine structural matches for possible shared functional machinery and informative differences. Keep each compared structure’s experimental or predicted origin, construct, chains, assembly, missing regions and uncertainty explicit. A prediction’s confidence describes the model; it is not a measure of similarity to another structure or evidence that a proposed activity was measured.

Retain actual structural-alignment scores, TM-score with its length normalization, DALI Z score, RMSD in angstroms, aligned-residue counts and coverage where reported. Preserve the atom or residue selections, aligned spans and method conventions. A low RMSD over a small fragment does not establish a full-protein match, and unlike structural statistics are not interchangeable.

Compare the catalytic residues, substrate-recognition pocket, loops, domain arrangement and partner interfaces that bear on the functions under consideration. A shared fold can identify a broad family while leaving exact chemistry unresolved; missing catalytic machinery or altered recognition features can favor another interpretation. Connect the comparator’s experimentally measured property to the actual structural correspondence. Keep structural compatibility distinct from measured target binding, catalysis, transport or physiological necessity, and preserve negative comparisons and unresolved specificity. Experimental ligand contacts or conformations remain separate observations from the structural resemblance used to transfer their meaning.

evidence.limit: Complete short primary paper and methods read. No ribB-neighborhood retrieval or enzymatic measurement repeated. | Group source-use limits: Auxotroph occurrence is compatible with salvage but does not measure native salvage flux. evidence.observation: MJ0056 has a riboflavin-kinase-like fold with bound CDP despite undetectable sequence similarity to known kinases. Its homologs are adjacent to ribB in multiple archaea. It also occurs in riboflavin auxotrophs, consistent with phosphorylation of salvaged vitamin rather than de novo riboflavin synthesis alone.
